best_for: Students and researchers who collect papers from the web and need clean citations in Word, LibreOffice or Google Docs without paying for a reference manager.
description:
Zotero is a reference manager made by Digital Scholar, a nonprofit that builds software for researchers and cultural heritage institutions, together with a global community of contributors. It is open source, and Zotero says it has no financial interest in your private data.

You can sort what you save into collections, tag it with keywords, or set up saved searches that fill themselves as your library grows. A built-in PDF reader lets you highlight and underline in color, then pull those annotations into a note. Each quote keeps a link to its page and a citation for your paper. If you turn on sync, your library can also be opened from any web browser. For a one-off bibliography, the free ZoteroBib site needs no install.

points.title: Save sources as you browse
points.text: The browser connector picks up articles, preprints, news stories and library books from the page you are on and files them in your library.

points.title: Citations where you write
points.text: Plugins for Word, LibreOffice and Google Docs insert citations and build the bibliography in any of more than 9,000 styles.

points.title: Sync is free, storage is not
points.text: Syncing your library records is free and unlimited. Attached files get 300 MB free; more is USD 20 a year for 2 GB, USD 60 for 6 GB or USD 120 for unlimited. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: WebDAV has a catch
points.text: You can sync files through your own WebDAV server instead of paying, but that only covers your personal library, not group libraries.

points.title: Shared libraries for teams
points.text: Groups let any number of people share a library at no cost. Zotero is AGPL-3.0 software from an independent nonprofit.

points.title: System needs
points.text: Zotero needs Windows 10 or later or macOS 10.15 or later. Windows installers are machine-wide for x86, x64 and Arm64, and the Windows listing keeps 80 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is unverified
points.text: The Linux build here is a Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 that Flathub does not mark as verified.
